description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is transaction.TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS, and this case is an add that the dataset refuses. Two independent sources say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and the online transaction inventory row '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |', which sits at README.md:315 in this checkout. Two citations for that row are in circulation and both are wrong: this file's authoring brief cites README.md:222, which is a spring-boot:run snippet, and sibling case19 cites README.md:224, which is not the row either. The verified line is :315, and it is corrected in the open rather than propagated, because a citation that does not resolve is worse than none (practices B1 and B4). Rule R1 governs the resolution - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - so the class keeps its mandated name and nothing is renamed. The mirror image is parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. No case in this folder is downgraded to read-only to match the name: the EXEC CICS WRITE at :713 is pinned at its full 350 bytes by both case19 and this case, and this is the one that proves the program hands over a complete record even when the dataset rejects it. PROVENANCE - STATICALLY DERIVED AND NEVER CAPTURED (practice B12): every expected value below was derived by reading app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl against the 350-byte layout of app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy, the symbolic-map input widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY and the real rows of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt. None of it was captured from a live COBOL run, because none is possible in this environment: the Agent Action Plan records at section 0.7.6 that the only available COBOL compiler reports 'indexed file handler : disabled', and TRANSACT is an indexed KSDS that this program browses backwards and then writes to, so neither the browse nor the write can execute here at all. That is risk R-A, and substituting a derived baseline for a captured one is declared rather than absorbed. WHY THIS CASE IS NOT A SECOND COPY OF case19 (practice B4): this file's authoring brief describes case20 as the canonical successful insert seeded with three rows - which is the scenario case19 already owns, down to the three seeded rows and the WRITE NORMAL arm. Rewriting case20 to match the brief would have produced two cases asserting one arm and left three arms with no owner at all: the READPREV DFHRESP(ENDFILE) empty-master path, the shared DFHRESP(DUPKEY)/DFHRESP(DUPREC) write arm, and the only FINAL_STATE assertion of an empty dataset in this folder. case19's own description delegates the first of those here in as many words - it records that case20 owns the ENDFILE arm and declares TRANSACT with the empty shape - so the duplication would also have broken a cross-reference a reviewer is entitled to rely on, and would have cost gate G47 its FileStatus '22' duplicate outcome on the write path. The distinct scenario is therefore kept and the brief's divergence is documented instead of silently resolved either way. Nothing is lost by keeping it: the four gates the brief attaches to case20 are all still proven right here, because the program composes and hands over a complete 350-byte record before the dataset refuses it - G19 on the record width, G21 on the trailing FILLER, and G23 with G24 on the scale and the rounding mode of TRAN-AMT. WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES: EIBCALEN is 218 and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives at '1', so NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :120 is false and :132 receives the map; EIBAID is DFHENTER, so the ordered EVALUATE at :133-152 takes its first arm at :134 and performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY (the REENTER state, gate G38). Both validation paragraphs pass: the account half of VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS resolves through the CXACAIX alternate index and takes the DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm of READ-CXACAIX-FILE, so CARDNIN is overwritten from XREF-CARD-NUM rather than typed; all eleven data fields are present, TTYPCD and TCATCD are numeric, TRNAMT satisfies the positional amount check, both dates are positionally valid and both CSUTLDTC calls at :393 and :413 report severity '0000' so the outer IFs at :397 and :417 accept outright (gate G12), and MID is numeric. CONFIRMI holds the LOWER-CASE 'y'. That matters on its own: the EVALUATE at :169 spells the accepting condition as two consecutive WHEN clauses over one action - WHEN 'Y' at :170 and WHEN 'y' at :171, both falling into PERFORM ADD-TRANSACTION at :172 - so the two spellings are equivalent by construction and not by accident. case19 takes that arm through 'Y' and this case takes it through 'y', which is the only way to show the fall-through is real rather than a single-literal test that happens to pass. THE IDENTIFIER GENERATOR ON AN EMPTY MASTER: :444 moves HIGH-VALUES into TRAN-ID and :445-447 position a backward browse past the end of the file, attempt to read the record carrying the highest key, and end the browse. STARTBR reports DFHRESP(NORMAL) and its arm at :653-654 is CONTINUE. READPREV then finds nothing, because TRANSACT is declared empty, and takes DFHRESP(ENDFILE) at :688-689, which moves ZEROS to TRAN-ID and - crucially - raises NO error flag. An empty file is a normal condition here, not a failure: with TRAN-ID zeroed, :448 moves nought into WS-TRAN-ID-N PIC 9(16), :449 adds one, and :451 renders it back into TRAN-ID PIC X(16) as sixteen zero-padded digits, so the first record ever written to an empty master carries TRAN-ID 0000000000000001. Getting that arm wrong is the difference between an empty master being loadable and being permanently unloadable, which is why it is pinned rather than assumed. The reachability is honest: no forced outcome is declared for the browse read at all, so the ENDFILE condition arises naturally from a genuinely empty dataset rather than being counterfeited by a stubbed status. TRANSACT is expressed as a declaration carrying its width and its copybook rather than as a tenth fixture file, because app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine files and none of them is a transaction file (Agent Action Plan section 0.4.9), so no tenth fixture is requested. ENDBR HAS NO ERROR PATH: ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE at :702-706 is a bare EXEC CICS ENDBR DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) with no RESP operand, no RESP2 operand and no EVALUATE after it. It has no outcome to drive and is never given an error expectation in any case in this folder. All three browse steps are genuinely reached here - the positioning at :445 succeeded and the ENDFILE arm raised no error flag - and the same three paragraphs serve a third caller, COPY-LAST-TRAN-DATA, which repeats the identical trio at :476-478 on the DFHPF5 arm, so no paragraph may assume who called it. THE RECORD, DERIVED FIELD BY FIELD FROM app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy (practices B8 and B11): :450 initialises the record area and :451-465 fill it. Offsets are summed mechanically from the PICTURE clauses, never inferred: TRAN-ID at 1-16 is X(16) rendered from WS-TRAN-ID-N 9(16) as sixteen zero-padded digits; TRAN-TYPE-CD at 17-18 is X(02) from TTYPCDI X(2) at the same width; TRAN-CAT-CD at 19-22 is 9(04) from TCATCDI X(4), an alphanumeric-to-numeric move; TRAN-SOURCE at 23-32 is X(10) from TRNSRCI X(10) at the same width; TRAN-DESC at 33-132 is X(100) receiving TDESCI X(60), so it is left-justified with 40 trailing spaces; TRAN-AMT at 133-143 is S9(09)V99, eleven bytes, nine integer digits and two decimal places with the sign overpunched into the trailing byte; TRAN-MERCHANT-ID at 144-152 is 9(09) from MIDI X(9); TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME at 153-202 is X(50) receiving MNAMEI X(30), so 20 trailing spaces; TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY at 203-252 is X(50) receiving MCITYI X(25), so 25 trailing spaces; TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP at 253-262 is X(10) from MZIPI X(10) at the same width; TRAN-CARD-NUM at 263-278 is X(16) from CARDNINI X(16), and its value is the one resolved from the cross-reference rather than the one typed; TRAN-ORIG-TS at 279-304 and TRAN-PROC-TS at 305-330 are each X(26) receiving a X(10) date; and FILLER at 331-350 is X(20). The widths sum 16+2+4+10+100+11+9+50+50+10+16+26+26+20 = 350, which is what app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy's own header records as 'RECLN = 350' and what gate G19 requires; the case pins both the ordered field map and the whole 350-byte image, so a dropped or mis-sized span fails on the total as well as on the field. THE TEN-BYTE DATE IN A TWENTY-SIX-BYTE TIMESTAMP, PRESERVED AND NEVER ENRICHED (practice B5): TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS are declared X(26), the width of a DB2-style YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmmmmm value as it appears elsewhere in this system, but :464-465 move in TORIGDTI and TPROCDTI, which app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY declares as X(10). Each stored field is therefore the ten-character date followed by exactly sixteen spaces. That is genuine legacy behaviour to reproduce, not a gap to fill: synthesising a time component would invent bytes the COBOL never writes and would change 350 bytes of observable output. FILLER, AND WHY THE INITIALIZE AT :450 DOES NOT REACH IT (gate G21): ISO COBOL's INITIALIZE deliberately ignores FILLER items, so INITIALIZE TRAN-RECORD at :450 sets the named fields and leaves bytes 331-350 holding whatever the record area already contained. In a case seeded with existing rows that is a real hazard, because the preceding READPREV would have deposited a previous record's trailing bytes there and the expectation would depend on which row the browse happened to land on. On this case's empty master that hazard does not exist at all: READPREV took the ENDFILE arm and no record was ever read into the area, so nothing can have been carried over, and the twenty bytes are the freshly acquired area's pad. The empty master therefore makes the FILLER expectation MORE deterministic than a seeded one, not less, and FILLER is pinned as twenty spaces. It is a first-class span with its own declared length in common.FixedWidthRecord rather than an implicit gap inferred between two named fields, and the pad byte is resolved through the named charset instead of a hard-coded 0x20, so an EBCDIC record would pad with its own space. Dropping FILLER would shorten the record to 330 bytes and move nothing - there is nothing behind it - but it would break the declared width, which is exactly the failure gates G19 and G21 exist to catch. NUMERIC POLICY (rules R2, R3 and R4; gates G23 and G24): TRNAMTI arrives as +00000012.34, matching the +99999999.99 mask the validation at :383-386 enforces, and :456-457 convert it with a second FUNCTION NUMVAL-C - the same intrinsic already applied to the same field during validation, which is why the re-edited screen form and the stored image must agree on one value. :458 stores the result into TRAN-AMT PIC S9(09)V99, giving the eleven-character zoned image 0000000123D: ten leading digits for 12.34 scaled to two decimal places, and a trailing D carrying the positive zoned overpunch for a final digit of 4, so the stored value is +12.34. The scale is exactly 2, taken from the PICTURE clause and not chosen, and the rounding mode is RoundingMode.DOWN through common.CobolDecimal - never HALF_UP, never HALF_EVEN, and never double or float - because the keyword ROUNDED appears zero times across all twenty-eight COBOL programs, so COBOL truncates excess fractional digits on store and truncation is the only faithful behaviour. THE WRITE AND ITS THREE ARMS, WITH THIS CASE ON THE DUPLICATE (gate G30, rule R7): WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE at :711-749 issues EXEC CICS WRITE DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) FROM(TRAN-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-RECORD) RIDFLD(TRAN-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-ID) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), then evaluates WS-RESP-CD over three arms in source order with WHEN OTHER last. This case forces the duplicate. The identifier is a high-water mark taken without a lock - the browse is read-only and the WRITE carries no UPDATE - so two operators adding at once can compute the same next key, which is precisely how a real duplicate arises and why the arm is worth pinning. DFHRESP(DUPKEY) at :735 and DFHRESP(DUPREC) at :736 are two WHEN clauses over a SINGLE action at :737-741: move 'Y' to WS-ERR-FLG, move the literal 'Tran ID already exist...' to WS-MESSAGE, move -1 to ACTIDINL and send. The literal reads 'exist', not 'exists'; the grammatical slip is part of the observable output and is reproduced rather than tidied (practice B5). That arm carries NO DISPLAY, so no console line is emitted and this case declares no DISPLAY_LINE message - which is a positive assertion, not an omission. It also sets no colour, so ERRMSGC keeps the map's default DFHDFCOL: :727 is the program's only attribute move anywhere and it belongs exclusively to the NORMAL arm, so gate G38's red-plus-'*' CSSETATY error highlight does not apply here either. The record is still reported on the WRITES channel, because the program did hand those 350 bytes to the dataset and the dataset refused them - an observation about the program - while the FINAL_STATE channel stays empty at a row count of zero, which is an observation about the dataset. Conflating the two would make a refused write indistinguishable from an accepted one. THE TWO SIBLING WRITE ARMS, DOCUMENTED HERE RATHER THAN GIVEN FILES OF THEIR OWN (gate G15 fixes this folder at twenty cases): DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :724-734 is case19's, and its order matters - :725 performs INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS FIRST, which blanks all fourteen input receivers and WS-MESSAGE and puts -1 back on ACTIDINL, so every field on the sent screen is empty; :726 blanks WS-MESSAGE; :727 moves DFHGREEN into ERRMSGC; and only THEN do :728-733 STRING the notice, which is why it survives the blanking that preceded it. Both literals carry a space at the joining edge - 'Transaction added successfully. ' ends with one and ' Your Tran ID is ' begins with one - so the notice holds TWO consecutive spaces after 'successfully.', and because a zero-filled sixteen-digit key contains no space, TRAN-ID DELIMITED BY SPACE contributes all sixteen digits before the closing full stop. WHEN OTHER at :742-748 is the third arm: it displays 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD - both operands are PIC S9(09) COMP at :47-48, so each renders as nine characters and COBOL concatenates the four operands with no separator, giving lines of the form RESP:000000019REAS:000000000 - then reports 'Unable to Add Transaction...' and moves -1 to ACTIDINL. All three arms are distinct messages and none may be crossed with the browse texts, 'Transaction ID NOT found...' at :657 and 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' at :664 and :693, or with the two cross-reference texts owned by case10 and case14. THE -1 TO ACTIDINL QUIRK, PRESERVED AND NEVER CORRECTED (practice B5): five error arms move -1 to ACTIDINL OF COTRN2AI - the two rejecting STARTBR arms at :659 and :666, the READPREV WHEN OTHER arm at :695, and both WRITE error arms at :740 and :747, the first of which is this case's. Every one of those messages is about a transaction, yet the cursor goes to the Account ID field. That is not a defect to tidy: app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY declares no transaction-identifier field at all, so the account field is the only place the program has to put the cursor, and redirecting it somewhere more sensible would change behaviour. ACTIDINL is a COMP PIC S9(4) length item, which makes it validation metadata rather than data: it travels as this case's cursorField and never as a JSON payload member. THE DFHPF5 PATH, DOCUMENTED HERE FOR ITS TRUNCATION DIRECTIONS (rule R5): the DFHPF5 arm at :146-147 performs COPY-LAST-TRAN-DATA at :471-495, which runs VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS, then moves HIGH-VALUES to TRAN-ID and repeats the same STARTBR, READPREV and ENDBR trio at :476-478 - the third invocation of those paragraphs - and, IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON, copies the last record back onto the screen at :481-492 before performing PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :495. Its moves run the opposite way to this case's and truncate rather than pad, and COBOL truncates a PIC X move on the RIGHT: TRAN-DESC X(100) into TDESCI X(60) keeps the first 60 bytes and discards 40; TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS X(26) into TORIGDTI and TPROCDTI X(10) keep the first 10 bytes, which is exactly the date and nothing else - the inverse of the pad this case performs; TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME X(50) into MNAMEI X(30) keeps 30; and TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY X(50) into MCITYI X(25) keeps 25. TRAN-AMT is routed through WS-TRAN-AMT-E PIC +99999999.99 at :481 before reaching TRNAMTI, so the screen form is the edited mask rather than the zoned image. THE INPUTS, BY BINDING KEY ONLY (gate G46): each dataset is named by its application.yml binding key rather than by dataset name, so not one fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in this file - the case model enforces it structurally, since its dataset-key pattern admits at most eight undotted upper-case characters and a dotted name cannot bind. CCXREF is seeded from cardxref.txt exactly as shipped, at 36 bytes per row, where CVACT03Y declares 50 as 16+9+11+14; the 36-to-50 pad of the trailing FILLER PIC X(14) is DECLARED as a normalisation and applied once at SEED time, so this case does not pre-pad a single row (gate G16, risk R-F). The pad has exactly one owner and it is worth naming correctly, because two sources state it wrongly: this file's brief and case19's description both credit parity/FieldDiffer. The verified owner is ParityCase.DatasetNormalisation.normaliseSeedRow, the single validated normaliser, which ParityHarness calls at seeding and never reimplements; FieldDiffer pads nothing at all - it treats a width disagreement as a difference and never invents bytes - so a case that forgets its normalisation fails loudly at seeding instead of being quietly repaired at comparison time. The account whose key is used, 00000000050, is a genuine row of the shipped fixture: cardxref.txt's first row carries card number 0500024453765740 with XREF-ACCT-ID 00000000050, which is why TRAN-CARD-NUM holds that card number and nothing invented. There is no separate CXACAIX seed, because CXACAIX is a PATH over the CCXREF base cluster: one seeded cluster answers both access paths as an alternate-index finder rather than as a second table (gate G45). ACCTDAT is seeded from acctdata.txt precisely to make visible what practice B5 requires be preserved - WS-ACCTDAT-FILE is declared at :40 and appears in no DATASET operand anywhere in the program, and COPY CVACT01Y at :89 is a dead include - so the file is opened by nothing and read by nothing. It is seeded and never touched, and no ACCTDAT entry appears in expectedWrites or expectedFinalState here or in any other case in this folder. NO REWRITE AND NO DELETE: TRANSACT is only ever browsed and written. No program in this codebase issues EXEC CICS REWRITE or EXEC CICS DELETE against it, so TransactionRepository deliberately declares neither operation - a repository offering them would be offering an access path the COBOL never had, and no case here can assert one. Nor is TRANSACT ever read by key in this program: the highest identifier comes from a backward browse, deliberately, because a keyed READ would need the key it is trying to discover. STATELESSNESS, THE CLOCK AND THE COMMAREA: all conversation state travels in the payload and none in a session (rule R6, gate G37) - the commarea arrives as a request member and leaves as the navigation map. It is the 160 bytes of COCOM01Y plus the separate 58-byte CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension declared at :72-80 as 16+16+8+1+1+16, which stays its own field and is never folded into NavigationContext, giving the 218 bytes EIBCALEN reports (practice B11). The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34 and both date inputs are the fixed literal 2022-07-18, never a computed today and never a captured timestamp (practice B7); the pinned instant is the program's own version footer, 'Ver: CardDemo_v1.0-15-g27d6c6f-68 Date: 2022-07-19 23:12:34 CDT' at :782, which is why POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :552-571 yields CURDATEO 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO 23:12:34 beside TRNNAMEO CT02, PGMNAMEO COTRN02C and the two COTTL01Y titles at PIC X(40). The charset is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). Because this arm does not call INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS, the sent screen RETAINS every value the operator typed, with CARDNINO showing the cross-reference-resolved card number - the opposite of case19's blanked form, and the reason the two cases must not share one expectation. :520 moves WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), losing the last two bytes, left-justified and space-padded, per rule R5, which is why the two expected messages are declared at 80 and 78 characters respectively. expectedReturnCode is 0 and jobParameters is empty: COTRN02C contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere, so no path here abends and gate G35 does not apply, just as G32 does not (the program has no GO TO), nor G39 (this screen paginates nothing), nor G43 (there is no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC), nor G40 (this arm returns with a TRANSID rather than transferring control). The response returns to COTRN02C through map COTRN2A of mapset COTRN02 with termination RETURN_TRANSID. GOVERNING RULES: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', and that single line is the whole document - confirmed directly rather than assumed. No user rule governs this file, and their absence is not licence to lower the bar: the enterprise practices of Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 bind instead, and the ones this case leans on are named where they apply above - B1 on placeholders and resolvable citations, B3 on the reference trees being read-only, B4 on documenting conflicts rather than silently correcting them, B5 on preserving legacy behaviour, B7 on a pinned clock, B8 on being explicit, B11 on offsets summed from the copybook, and B12 on honest provenance. The unit is invoked as a plain constructed controller with no MockMvc, no HTTP and no JobLauncher in the path, so the arithmetic and the arm selection are asserted directly (gate G51).
